title: Decca date, pneumonia and Harold West on drums
summary: Roy made a Decca session, caught pneumonia, and replaced Zutty with Harold West, who could not read.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Oh, while I was there ...[AIRPLANE OVERHEAD] Barron(?) comes to see me...
That's while you were still in Chicago?

I was working at the Deuces. But you see, I had one record contract with Decca. We made the one date, you know, with "After You've Gone" and that on it, and then they had the band. And buying(?) the band, I got pneumonia

and went to the hospital. So in the meantime, Zutty was giving everybody such a bad time, and I had just started progressing a little, getting out of the woodwork, and was (?) and "Let's get rid of Zutty" and all that. I didn't know what was going on with it.

I know when I came out, he was gone. Harold West was there. And my brother's in the band now, you know, and he's writing music, and he writes for the drums, too. He's got things they have to play. But Harold couldn't read no kind of way, you know. He was a good swinger, though. So I just told him. I said, "Look, Harold, you got the gig. While you're here, take some lessons, because sometimes we might get a job or you might have to play something outside of 'I Got Rhythm'." And he said, "Yeah," and he was supposed to be taking... When I asked him once, he said, "Well, I'm taking drums off of Frank Trenier(?)." He was like the band-boy for Gene Krupa, really, and he later became the manager, you know. But he fancied himself as a little drummer, you know. But he didn't ...[CAR NOISE]...

So it played out like this. We had a gig down in Stony Island. I think Stony Island is in Illinois, isn't it? Yeah. We had a night to play, a couple of nights to play, and one was an adagio dancing night. And they had some Classical music. It was very (?), but I was reading ..(?)..

We just [SINGS]... I forget the name of it. [SINGS 8 BARS] And they had some different changes in tempos, you know, one of those things. And West couldn't get it, so I had to end up playing it on the drums. "Well," I said, "I told you this would happen."

Then we finally decided to break out of there. By this time, Joe had quit and went back to New York. Yeah. Freddie Bowman(?) was in now. Scoops is gone now; Scoops had gone with Earl, I think -- Earl or Fletcher.
